route: Frankfurt → Central European Branch Office → Munich
intro:
The morning began under a gloomy, overcast sky as I made my way to Selters, Germany, for my final Bethel visit of this European adventure. Despite the gray weather, I was looking forward to the day. After visiting several branch offices throughout this trip, it felt fitting to conclude this part of the journey at the Central European branch.

Arriving at Bethel was refreshing. There is something special about visiting these facilities in different countries. Each location has its own character, history, and surroundings, yet they all share the same purpose and spirit.

My tour began with the Bethel Life exhibit, which provided a glimpse into life at the branch and the people who serve there. It was wonderful to see the personal experiences and learn more about the work being accomplished.

Next was Never Alone, an exhibit highlighting the experiences of Jehovah’s Witnesses during World War II and the years that followed. It was a moving reminder of the courage, faith, and endurance shown during some of the most difficult periods in history.

The final exhibit focused on the Bible, particularly its history in Germany. Seeing the historical displays, including information about Gutenberg’s printing press and the collection of Bibles, was fascinating. Germany played such an important role in the history of Bible printing and distribution, making this a particularly meaningful place to explore that history.

Another highlight was seeing the branch’s printery in operation. Watching the printing equipment at work and seeing the magazines and other publications being produced was impressive. It was fascinating to see the process firsthand, including the machinery cutting the newly printed tracts. Seeing the scale and organization of the work gave me an even greater appreciation for everything involved.

I also enjoyed lunch at Bethel and had the opportunity to spend some time with a friend, visiting them in their department. These personal connections have been among the most memorable parts of my travels.

After leaving Selters, it was time to begin the long drive south toward Munich. The weather remained gray, and rain accompanied portions of the journey. I passed through Nuremberg without stopping, continuing along the Autobahn toward my final destination.

By the time I reached Munich, I was ready to settle in. Arriving at the Hilton near the airport, I received a pleasant surprise: an upgrade to a suite! After so many days on the road, it was a wonderful way to spend my final nights in Germany.

Tomorrow would bring another adventure, with plans to visit Liechtenstein, the final country remaining on my list. With the journey quickly approaching its conclusion, there was a growing sense that The Long Way Around was finally coming full circle.

Looking back on the day, what stood out most wasn’t the distance traveled or the places visited, but the people. From one branch office to another, across different countries and languages, I’ve been reminded of something truly special: wherever we go in the world, we’re never far from family.
